title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC0LE_1RD1RA_0RE1RF_1LF0RC_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC0LE_1RD1RA_0RE1RF_1LF0RC_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. This page describes what its run looks like at the level of words and counters, what a halt would need, and what is still missing. The description comes from simulation (first look, about an hour of study); nothing beyond the bounded runs is proved.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps, the C simulator none in 109. The macro structure described below is observed in the simulation, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 24,776 cells have been visited and 14,654 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.189). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Nested counters
claims.text: Runs of 1 0^2 and of 1 0 1^2 0 grouped by markers 1 0 1^2 0^2; the first a-run grows by 6 while the first c-run shrinks by 2 between consecutive samples shown in the README (observed up to 10<sup>9</sup> steps).

claims.title: Slow growth
claims.text: Only the left side grows, 27,455 cells at 1.86·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

claims.title: Shift rules, for every n
claims.text: C crosses (100)^n to the right and leaves (110)^n; A crosses (001)^n and leaves (101)^n; E crosses (11010)^n and leaves (01010)^n.

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 8 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 18,577 to 133,374 visited cells and compresses to 17 to 36 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Proposed family: F06, block-list counters
claims.text: The description grows slowly: 19, 24, 36 and 35 level-2 tokens at the left-end records at 2.8·108, 109, 4.2·109 and 1.6·1010 steps. At the last one the tape is a block (010)^1537, then a list of blocks of the words 10101 and 100 (3 to 1,184 copies each) closed by markers 1010 (01)^3, and a last block (10101)^21602. A list of units of the same form whose number grows slowly is a list of counters (F06) and not a bounded description (F01): the token count nearly doubled on the screen.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No macro rule has been proved for this machine yet; see the README's Later section for the next steps.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The tape is made of two words in runs that behave like nested counters; the outermost counter grows to the left, slowly.

facts.text: runs of two words behave like the levels of a counter
No halt in the C simulator; 24,776 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Nested counters
html: Write a for 1 0^2 and c for 1 0 1^2 0. When the head is at the left end in state A, the tape reads, for example at step 513,296,770, A>0 0 1 0 1 0 a^465 1 0 c^86 1 0 1^2 0^2 a^21 1 0 a 1 0 c^8 1 0 1^2 0^2 a^7 1 0 a 1 0 c^63 1 0 1^2 0^2 a 1 0 a 1 0 c^1454 1^2 0 c^3018 1 0 1: runs of a and runs of c, grouped by the marker 1 0 1^2 0^2.

From one such sample to the next shown here (a few samples apart) the first run of a grows by 6 while the first run of c shrinks by 2, and the runs further right change more rarely, like the digits of a counter with several levels. The tape grows only to the left, and slowly (triage exponent 0.19): 27,455 cells at 1.86·109 steps.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine halts when it reads a 1 in state F (F1 is the halting transition). F is entered from D on a 1 (D1 = 1RF) and from E on a 0 (E0 = 1LF).

sections.heading: Shift rules over the runs
html: Runs of a and of c are crossed by shift rules proved for every length: C over (100)^n leaves (110)^n, A over (001)^n leaves (101)^n, and E over (11010)^n leaves (01010)^n. The counter map between left-end samples was not found.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.
Proposed family: F06, block-list counters (a slowly growing list of units made of two words).

The description grows slowly: 19, 24, 36 and 35 level-2 tokens at the left-end records at 2.8·108, 109, 4.2·109 and 1.6·1010 steps. At the last one the tape is a block (010)^1537, then a list of blocks of the words 10101 and 100 (3 to 1,184 copies each) closed by markers 1010 (01)^3, and a last block (10101)^21602.
A list of units of the same form whose number grows slowly is a list of counters (F06) and not a bounded description (F01): the token count nearly doubled on the screen.
Next step. The round rule on the list of pairs (a, b), sampled at the left-end records, and the rule that adds a unit.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.189). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 24,776 cells (260 left of the start, 24,423 right), with a density of 1s of 0.591.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: nested counters built from two words, growing left
summary: The tape is made of two words, 1 0^2 and 1 0 1^2 0, in runs separated by markers 1 0 1^2 0^2; the runs behave like nested counters, the outermost run on the left growing while inner ones are used up.
